title: What it takes to train a frontier model
blurb: A tour of what goes into training a 2026 frontier model: data, scaling, chips, parallelism, failures, post-training and cost.
description: A frontier model is a file of numbers, but producing it takes tens of trillions of tokens, tens of thousands of chips and a great deal of engineering. Using only 2026 reports (GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K2.5, a Meta fault-tolerance paper and Epoch AI data), the film follows data, scaling, hardware, failures, post-training and cost, and flags what is an estimate.
takeaways: Pre-training reads tens of trillions of tokens, and most raw web text is filtered out before it is used.
A common rule of thumb puts training compute at about six times the active parameters times the tokens.
At 100,000 GPUs a failure arrives roughly every 18 minutes, so fault tolerance matters as much as raw speed.
Post-training now runs on huge fleets of sandboxed environments, and reward design is part of the job.
None of the three reports gives GPU hours or dollar costs, so cost can only be estimated from the buildout.
